extracted.intended_audience: writers participating in the NYC Midnight 100-word Microfiction Challenge (microfiction contest entrants)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing original microfiction (no more than 100 words) under a 24-hour time limit, following randomly assigned genre, action, and word prompts, for submission to the NYC Midnight 100-word Microfiction Challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: short stories no longer than 100 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be short stories no longer than 100 words (referred to on the page as a '100-word story').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition repeatedly describes the task as a 100-word story; entrants should ensure the final submission conforms to the 100-word limit (no longer than 100 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-hour time limit to craft story
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have 24 hours to craft their entry for each round of the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounds are timeboxed (e.g., 1st Round March 20–21); stories must be created/submitted during the assigned 24-hour window for that round.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomly assigned genre, action, and word
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 1st Round writers are placed randomly in groups and are assigned a genre, action, and word assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must write to the specific genre prompt they are given; the assignment is provided at the start of the round and must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: assigned action must take place in the story
rubrics_metrics.description: The assigned action must occur within the submitted story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not sufficient to merely mention the action; the story must depict the assigned action taking place.

rubrics_metrics.name: assigned word must be incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: The assigned word must be incorporated into the submitted story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories must include the assigned word as part of the 100-word text; follow any official rules about exact spelling/capitalization if specified in the Official Rules & Participation Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: originality of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be original stories created by the entrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes 'original' story — entries should not be plagiarized or previously published (see Official Rules & Participation Agreement for full IP/eligibility specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: judging and advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges select the top 15 in each group from the 1st Round to advance to the 2nd Round; from the 2nd Round judges select the top eight in each group to advance to the Final Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement is determined by judges' selections rather than an automatic scoring formula; judges' evaluation determines who moves forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: judge feedback provided for every submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback from the judges is provided for every submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every entrant will receive judge feedback on their submission; additionally a special review forum is available for participants to get peer reviews during the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: retention of author rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers retain all rights to the stories they create during the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organizers state they would not share stories publicly without consent; entrants keep copyright/rights to their work (see Official Rules & Participation Agreement for any usage/permission clauses).

rubrics_metrics.name: use of community peer review forum
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are encouraged to use an online forum to post and review stories and discuss the challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A vibrant community and special review forum exist for participants to receive peer feedback; using that forum is recommended but not mandatory for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: structural guidance — beginning, middle, and end
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice: even in microfiction, aim to craft a beginning, middle, and end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to 'Writing a Beginning, Middle, and End in Microfiction' as a recommended approach to structure tiny stories effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: character arc in microfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice: aim to create a character arc even within a very short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to 'Writing a Character Arc in Microfiction' — judges and readers value clear character change or development in constrained word counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: crafting effective plot twists
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice: techniques for crafting plot twists that work in short stories/microfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site offers a 'Plot Twists in Short Stories' resource suggesting plot twists can be used in microfiction; use with care so twists feel earned within the brief text.

rubrics_metrics.name: anatomy/strategies for resonant microfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level strategies to craft tiny stories that resonate universally (from experienced winners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Anatomy of Microfiction' article lists five strategies from a two-time winner — use those best-practice techniques to maximize resonance and impact in 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: registration and deadline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must register and meet entry deadlines (early entry and final entry deadlines are specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists Early Entry Deadline and Final Entry Deadline and recommends marking calendars (also notes emails may go to spam). Failure to register/enter by deadlines will prevent participation in the round.
